skill.name: ci-cd-security
skill.description: Reviews GitHub Actions YAML for dangerous triggers, excessive permissions, injection paths, unpinned actions, unsafe caches, artifact trust failures, and release risks.
skill.summary: Audit GitHub Actions workflows with a nine-pass, read-only security review and concrete remediation guidance.
skill.author: superagent-ai

security_audit.summary: All 65 static findings are false positives caused by security terminology, Markdown backticks, or illustrative workflow snippets. The skill performs read-only YAML review, requests no credentials, and contains no prompt injection or hidden execution intent.

content.value_statement: GitHub Actions workflows can expose credentials, repositories, and releases through subtle configuration errors. This skill applies a structured security review and proposes concrete fixes.
actual_capabilities: Reviews workflow triggers for privileged execution of untrusted code.
Checks workflow and job permissions for excessive GITHUB_TOKEN access.
Identifies mutable action references and recommends full commit SHA pinning.
Finds direct interpolation of attacker-controlled values into shell steps.
Evaluates checkout, cache, artifact, release, and self-hosted runner risks.
Groups findings by P0 through P3 severity and provides remediation guidance.
limitations: Performs static review of provided YAML and does not execute security tools.
Cannot inspect repository or organization settings without supplied evidence.
Cannot verify action ownership, pinned commits, or remote source behavior without external access.
Does not assess application code, dependency vulnerabilities, or runtime infrastructure.

use_cases.title: Review a pull request workflow
use_cases.description: Find unsafe triggers, shell interpolation, and token permissions before a workflow change merges.

use_cases.title: Harden release automation
use_cases.description: Assess publishing workflows for long-lived tokens, cache poisoning, missing environments, and absent provenance.

use_cases.title: Triage workflow risk at scale
use_cases.description: Apply a consistent severity model across workflow findings and prioritize the most exploitable paths.

prompt_templates.title: Basic workflow review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this GitHub Actions workflow for security issues. Group findings by severity and explain each recommended change.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner wants a complete review of one workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Check untrusted input
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect this workflow for attacker-controlled values entering shell steps, environment files, outputs, artifacts, or checkout references.
prompt_templates.scenario: A developer suspects template or artifact injection.

prompt_templates.title: Harden a release workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this release workflow for permissions, token usage, environments, cache poisoning, action pinning, attestations, and tag protections.
prompt_templates.scenario: A release engineer is preparing package publication.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze a workflow chain
prompt_templates.prompt: Trace trust boundaries across these linked workflows. Identify privileged paths from fork input, artifacts, caches, metadata, and self-hosted runners.
prompt_templates.scenario: A security engineer is reviewing a multi-workflow attack surface.

output_examples.input: Review a pull request workflow that places the pull request title directly in a shell step.
output: P0: The pull request title is attacker-controlled and enters the shell command.
Impact: A crafted title can execute commands with the job permissions.
Recommendation: Pass the title through an environment variable and quote it in the shell.

output_examples.input: Audit a package release workflow that uses a repository token and dependency caching.
output: P0: Dependency caching can carry poisoned content into the release path.
P2: A long-lived registry token increases credential exposure.
Recommendation: Remove release caching and use trusted publishing with a protected environment.

output_examples.input: Check a pull request test workflow with read-only permissions and commit-pinned actions.
output_examples.output: No findings against the standard rule set. Repository settings, action source behavior, and dependency runtime behavior were not verified.

best_practices: Provide complete workflow files so triggers, permissions, and job relationships remain visible.
Include linked workflows when artifacts, caches, or workflow_run events cross trust boundaries.
Verify suggested commit pins and repository settings through trusted administrative sources.
anti_patterns: Do not treat a clean YAML scan as proof that the complete CI/CD system is secure.
Do not hide attacker-controlled workflow values behind quoting without separating them from shell source.
Do not grant broad permissions to simplify remediation for a single workflow step.

faq.question: Does this skill run external scanners?
faq.answer: No. It reads supplied workflow YAML and applies documented review rules without installing or executing tools.

faq.question: Can it review multiple connected workflows?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide every linked workflow so it can trace artifacts, caches, permissions, and privileged event chains.

faq.question: Does it verify action commit hashes?
faq.answer: No. It detects pinning format, but remote ownership and commit legitimacy require trusted external verification.

faq.question: Can it inspect GitHub organization settings?
faq.answer: Only when you provide the settings as evidence. Workflow YAML cannot reveal organization policies or repository protections.

faq.question: What does a P0 finding mean?
faq.answer: P0 identifies a directly exploitable path where untrusted input can affect secrets, repository contents, or releases.

faq.question: Does a clean result guarantee security?
faq.answer: No. Action internals, dependencies, runner state, remote settings, and runtime behavior remain outside the YAML review.
